title: Agenticdse: A Multi-Agent Design Space Exploration Framework with Multi-Phase Bayesian Optimization for Chiplet Accelerators
evidence_span: AgenticDSE uses an exploration orchestrator, architecture analyst, and optimization engineer to refine chiplet-accelerator design spaces and perform phase-wise Bayesian exploration with ensemble surrogates; the official description reports 36.9% lower average distance to the Pareto front, 66% greater Pareto-front diversity, and 46x/18x reductions in input/output token use versus prior LLM-based solutions.
problem: Chiplet accelerator design-space exploration is complex, and black-box Bayesian optimization lacks domain knowledge while LLM-based exploration can consume excessive tokens.
method_or_artifact: Three cooperating LLM agents, analysis-driven search-space refinement, phase-wise Bayesian optimization, and ensemble surrogate modeling.
workload_or_benchmark: Chiplet accelerators for LLM inference; design objectives, accelerator templates, exploration budget, and Pareto objective definitions are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Chiplet-based accelerator architectures with a multi-objective PPA/interconnect design space; chiplet technology, packaging, and evaluation tools are unspecified.
metrics: 36.9% reduction in average distance to real Pareto front
limits: The description omits agent prompts, surrogate features, design objectives, exploration budgets, and accelerator/tool identities.
Pareto distance and diversity depend on the sampled design space and reference front; transfer beyond the tested chiplet templates is unknown.
Official description only; agent outputs and DSE reproducibility require paper-level verification.

title: An Adaptive Prediction of Tokens Fluctuation for Decoupled Prefetching to Accelerate Long-Context LLM Decoding
evidence_span: The paper uses adaptive prediction of token fluctuation, reuse-based recovery for evicted KV entries, and decoupled prefetching that overlaps transfer with attention; the official description says a 256-token cache matches full-KV accuracy and reports 2.50x average end-to-end speedup on long-context decoding.
problem: Long-context LLM decoding saturates memory bandwidth with KV accesses; static prediction can permanently evict useful tokens and synchronous scoring stalls the pipeline.
method_or_artifact: Adaptive token-fluctuation prediction, reuse-based recovery, and a decoupled prefetching architecture that hides data-transfer latency.
workload_or_benchmark: Long-context LLM decoding; models, context lengths, cache hierarchy, and accuracy metric are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: KV cache with a constrained 256-token resident cache and overlapped data movement; processor, memory bandwidth, and interconnect are unspecified.
metrics: Full-KV accuracy matched with 256 resident tokens
limits: The description omits model suite, context lengths, predictor overhead, bandwidth, cache policy, and accuracy tolerance.
Speedup and accuracy depend on token fluctuation distributions and hardware transfer overlap.
Official description only; cache-quality and latency claims require paper-level verification.

title: Semi-Virtual Addressing to Enhance Memory Safety on Microcontrollers
evidence_span: Semi-virtual addressing adds a deterministic Lightweight Address Translation Module without page tables, expanding the RISC-V CORE-V-MCU from 575 KB physical space to 2 GB effective address space; the description demonstrates heap randomization and type-safe allocation for memory protection.
problem: Microcontrollers lack virtual addressing for strong memory protection, while a full MMU adds cost and unpredictable latency.
method_or_artifact: Computation-based address translation through a page-table-free Lightweight Address Translation Module, integrated with heap randomization and type-safe allocation.
workload_or_benchmark: RISC-V CORE-V-MCU memory-protection use cases; application workload, latency measurements, and security evaluation are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Microcontroller-class RISC-V core with 575 KB physical address space and deterministic translation hardware; implementation area, timing, and memory technology are unspecified.
metrics: 575 KB physical address space expanded to 2 GB semi-virtual address space
Heap randomization and type-safe allocation demonstrated qualitatively
limits: The description omits translation area/latency, protection coverage, attack model, software compatibility, and baseline measurements.
Address-space expansion is not equivalent to a full MMU's isolation or operating-system semantics.
Official description only; security and implementation claims require paper-level verification.

title: Photomt : Accelerating Zero-Knowledge Proofs with a Photonic-Electronic Merkle Tree Engine
evidence_span: PhotoMT combines a photonic microring-resonator matrix-vector engine with digital control for Poseidon-hash Merkle-tree construction, using multi-subtree interleaving and an S-BOX bypass queue; the official description reports 18.8–20.5x throughput over ASIC designs and 3–5 orders of magnitude CPU-baseline energy-efficiency gain.
problem: Poseidon hashes dominate Merkle-tree construction in zero-knowledge proofs, creating throughput and energy bottlenecks.
method_or_artifact: Photonic-electronic collaborative Merkle-tree engine, photonic matrix-vector multiplication, multi-subtree interleaving, and S-BOX bypass scheduling.
workload_or_benchmark: Zero-knowledge-proof Merkle-tree construction with Poseidon hashes; proof sizes, hash parameters, and throughput/energy measurement boundary are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Photonic microring-resonator array plus digital control circuits; optical loss, process, ADC/DAC, thermal, and packaging assumptions are unspecified.
metrics: 3–5 orders of magnitude energy-efficiency gain over CPU baseline
limits: The description omits optical-device parameters, precision, conversion overhead, proof configuration, and ASIC comparison conditions.
CPU and ASIC energy boundaries may exclude supporting control, memory, and photonic I/O costs.
Official description only; photonic feasibility and cryptographic correctness require paper-level verification.

title: Rememtier: Rethinking Memory Tiering for CXL-Based SSD via Large Granularity Memory Access
evidence_span: WA-RMT dedicates CXL DRAM as a fast tier for main applications while isolating auxiliary tasks in host memory; its Sparse-burst Resistant Page Replacement Policy separates transient bursts from hot pages and uses cacheable/streamed CXL.io accesses with reordering. The official description reports up to 35% lower execution time and over 60% lower swap-in latency on mixed K-means, Radiosity, and ResNet50 workloads.
problem: Mixed datacenter workloads cause memory contention, page swapping, and memory pollution when auxiliary tasks interfere with primary applications.
method_or_artifact: Workload-aware reversed memory tiering, sparse-burst-resistant page replacement, and CXL.io access modes with data reordering.
workload_or_benchmark: Mixed K-means, Radiosity, and ResNet50 workloads; contention levels, memory capacities, CXL SSD/DRAM configuration, and baseline tiering policy are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: CXL SSD plus CXL DRAM fast tier and host memory; CXL generation, link topology, device firmware, and software stack are unspecified.
limits: The description omits CXL device latency/bandwidth, capacity ratios, workload mixes, page sizes, and baseline tuning.
Results may depend on the chosen burst patterns and fast-tier allocation policy.
Official description only; system-level memory and software overheads require paper-level verification.
